findings.title: var.readers is granted roles/spanner.databaseUser, which includes write access
findings.explanation: The variable, resource and example service account are all named and described as readers, but roles/spanner.databaseUser grants read and write (DML, mutations, partitioned DML, transactions). Every member a caller puts in 'readers' can modify or delete data. HLD_GCP_178/210 only check for public and default service-account members, not whether the role matches the stated intent. Members are also not checked for a valid IAM principal prefix.
findings.remediation: Grant roles/spanner.databaseReader to var.readers, and add a separate var.writers list for roles/spanner.databaseUser so read-write access is an explicit choice. Validate that members carry an IAM principal prefix.

findings.title: Example instance_name "pike" violates the Spanner 6-30 character name rule; the module does not validate it
findings.explanation: The google provider documents that a Spanner instance name must be 6-30 characters, and display_name (set from the same variable) must be 4-30. "pike" is 4 characters, so the example plans cleanly but fails at apply. var.instance_name and var.database_name only check for non-empty strings, so invalid IDs are caught by the API rather than at plan time.
findings.remediation: Validate var.instance_name against ^[a-z][-a-z0-9]{4,28}[a-z0-9]$ and var.database_name against ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,28}[a-z0-9]$, and rename the example instance to a valid name.

findings.title: Example never grants the Spanner service agent access to the CMEK key, so database creation fails
findings.explanation: The module requires a CMEK key and passes it to google_spanner_database.main.encryption_config. Spanner encrypts through its service agent (service-<project-number>@gcp-sa-spanner.iam.gserviceaccount.com), which needs roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key. The example creates the key but no IAM binding, and nothing orders the database after such a binding, so the database create is rejected.
findings.remediation: In the example, add a google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member granting roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter to the Spanner service agent and pass the key ID to the module through that resource, so the grant exists before the database is created.

findings.title: CMEK key is a single free-form string with no format or location check against the instance config
findings.explanation: Spanner requires the CMEK key to live in the same location as a regional instance config, and multi-region configs need one key per replica region (encryption_config.kms_key_names). The module accepts any non-empty string and only supports kms_key_name, so a key in the wrong region or a multi-region config fails at apply, after the instance has already been created.
findings.remediation: Validate var.kms_key_name as a full CryptoKey resource ID, and add a precondition that, for regional-<region> configs, the key's location matches <region>.
